A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching, including discussion relocated from the appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual reasoning experiments, activation interventions, layer-wise analyses, and comparisons with supervised fine-tuning and PPO.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds PolyMath evaluation results in Appendix G.3 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The language-subspace decomposition, SVD procedure, activation subtraction, and upper-layer reinjection remain unchanged. Renaming activation ablation as language–reasoning disentanglement and specifying layer ranges do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3 adds human-verified PolyMath evaluation across three difficulty levels, extending the existing mathematical reasoning coverage. The original benchmarks and the same 11 evaluation languages are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, including unmodified backbones, SFT, and PPO. PolyMath extends the existing comparison between unmodified models and their intervened counterparts to another benchmark.

E3.justification: PolyMath introduces random sampling of 50 questions per difficulty level per language and difficulty-weighted accuracy. Figure 13 expands the displayed layer sweeps from 0–24 to 0–32 for Qwen-3-8B and from 4–28 to 0–44 for R1-Distill-Qwen-14B. These reported changes do not establish whether earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G.3 adds a robustness check motivated by dataset difficulty and translation quality, although it does not isolate their individual effects. Figure 13(c,d) revises the existing layer-wise analysis. The earlier activation-strength and representation-space analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly reports significance testing and gains with p < 0.05 on most benchmarks. It does not specify the test, individual comparisons, repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals, so the addition is limited statistical reporting rather than a documented increase in experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds PolyMath results, including Qwen-2.5-Instruct-7B average accuracy of 19.51 without intervention and 22.47 with intervention. Table 1 changes the Qwen-3-4B Bengali entry from 0.688 to 68.8, and Figure 13(c,d) revises plotted results. Most earlier results remain unchanged. The new R1 intervention average is reported as 43.31, whereas its listed language scores have an arithmetic mean of 43.61.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and Appendix C's decomposition and orthogonality procedure are retained. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or mathematical definition is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: language and reasoning can be disentangled, activation intervention improves multilingual reasoning, and the training-free approach can compete with post-training. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix G.3 newly interprets smaller high-resource language gaps on PolyMath in terms of dataset quality and difficulty, while persistent Swahili and Telugu deficits suggest structural capability disparities. Earlier discussions of the English anchor, fidelity trade-offs, and latent reasoning remain, with some moved into Section 6.

D1.justification: New Table 4 specifies total layers and middle/upper intervention ranges for all ten models. The abstract adds a code-repository link, and the checklist reports supplementary code and data. These improve documented access and implementation detail; the existing extraction procedure and SFT/PPO hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2025) as a decomposition reference and Chen et al. (2025b) on abstract thought beyond language, while removing Fedorenko et al. (2011). The general research positioning remains unchanged; the Coconut discussion and LENS citation were already present.

P1.justification: Terminology is standardized around disentanglement, two existing appendix discussions move into a new main-text Section 6, and acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added. Most scientific prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 5, redraws Figure 13(c,d) with revised curves and layer axes, and updates table labels and captions. Figures 3–4 now explain their existing dashed baseline lines. The remaining figures and the overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit intervention ranges and added code-access information improve reproducibility documentation, while PolyMath supplies useful evidence on harder multilingual mathematics. These are limited gains: significance testing and difficulty weights remain underspecified, and Table 5 introduces an unexplained average discrepancy. The core method and conclusions remain stable.
